description: The complete set of fixed system sentences a public-v2 projection may emit in a field marked `x-panshi-system-label: true`, keyed by field name. A system label describes the system (why a list is empty, why a value is null, why a chapter is held); it is not a claim about the character or the market and carries no truth class. A value outside its field's list is a contract violation: consumers and audits reject it rather than render it. `nonClaimNumberKeys` names the numeric keys that are provenance, versioning or scene layout rather than claims, and so carry no truth class either; every other number in a projection is covered by its own `truthClass` or a sibling `<field>TruthClass`.

requiredSiblingTruthClasses.note: Every property `x` that a public-v2.yaml schema pairs with a sibling property `xTruthClass`, keyed by that schema. Wherever an object of that schema carries a non-null `x`, it must carry its own non-null `xTruthClass`; it never falls back to the object's `truthClass` (2.2.0: nothing borrows identity from an outer or neighbouring class). A string value pins the class the sibling must equal; null means the contract lets the class vary with the source, so any class the slice allows is accepted, but the sibling itself is still mandatory. A displayed person's name and relationship label are authored chassis, so they are pinned to `fictional_setting` wherever the schema gives them a sibling. The audit re-derives the schema/property pairs from public-v2.yaml and refuses if this map and the contract disagree.
